results.authors: Wingerchuk DM, Banwell B, Bennett JL, et al.
results.summary: AQP4-IgG-positive NMOSD requires one core clinical characteristic (optic neuritis, acute myelitis, area postrema syndrome, acute brainstem, diencephalic or cerebral syndrome). Seronegative NMOSD requires two core characteristics with supporting MRI, including longitudinally extensive myelitis of three or more contiguous segments. Cell-based assays are recommended for AQP4-IgG.
results.title: International consensus diagnostic criteria for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders

results.authors: Banwell B, Bennett JL, Marignier R, et al.
results.summary: MOGAD requires a core demyelinating event, MOG-IgG by cell-based assay and exclusion of a better diagnosis. Supporting features include bilateral or anterior optic neuritis with disc oedema and perineural enhancement, conus involvement and ADEM-like lesions; CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands are uncommon.
results.title: Diagnosis of myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease: International MOGAD Panel proposed criteria

results.authors: Montalban X, Lebrun-Frenay C, Oh J, et al.
results.summary: The optic nerve is a fifth region shown by MRI, OCT or VEP; lesions in four or five regions establish dissemination in space without a separate test of dissemination in time; CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands or a raised kFLC index count as positive CSF. MS cord lesions are typically short and peripheral.

output.summary: Optic neuritis and myelitis occur in MS, NMOSD and MOGAD. AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG by cell-based assay, cord lesion length (three or more segments in NMOSD; short peripheral lesions in MS), brain lesion pattern and CSF oligoclonal bands (present in most people with MS, uncommon in NMOSD and MOGAD) separate the three. Natalizumab and fingolimod have been associated with worsening of NMOSD.

patient.history_present_illness:
Ms. Priya Sharma is a 31-year-old right-handed South Asian woman who presents to the neurology inpatient service for evaluation of painful vision loss in her right eye and progressive lower extremity weakness. She was in her usual state of health until approximately 16 days ago, when she developed periorbital pain behind her right eye that worsened with eye movement. Over the following 2 to 3 days, she noticed blurring and central haziness in her right visual field, with difficulty reading text on her computer screen. She initially attributed this to eye strain from her laboratory work and deferred medical attention. The visual symptoms plateaued and remain at roughly the same level over the past 10 days.

Approximately 10 days ago, she began noticing a new sensation of heaviness and stiffness in her left leg, initially subtle but now clearly interfering with her walking. She reports a band-like tightening sensation around her mid-torso at approximately the level of her navel. Over the past week she has developed urinary urgency with one episode of near-incontinence. She endorses intermittent electric shock-like sensations shooting down her spine and into both legs when she flexes her neck, which began about one week ago. She has noticed that her right eye vision worsens transiently after her morning shower, returning to baseline after several minutes.

Her husband brought her to the emergency department yesterday after she stumbled while walking and he observed her left foot dragging; she is now admitted to the neurology service for further evaluation.

On direct questioning, she recalls a brief episode of blurry vision in her right eye approximately three years ago lasting about one week that was attributed to fatigue by her general practitioner. She did not receive an ophthalmologic evaluation at that time and the episode resolved spontaneously. She denies prior limb weakness, paresthesias, bowel dysfunction, fever, oral ulcers, skin rash, joint pains, hiccups, nausea, or vomiting. She has no personal history of autoimmune disease and no family history of demyelinating disease. She is planning to start a family in the coming years and is very concerned about treatment implications.
